 Shri Bhashkar Agrawal, Advocate appearing on behalf o
 Gupta, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.

Order 
As per the office note, notices have been served on all the respondents; however, they have not entered their appearance except the Insurance Company.

2. The appellants have filed this Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 23.01.2012 passed by the learned V Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.) in Claim Case No.39/2010.
2.1 The appeal challenges the part of the award where the Insurance Company has been completely exonerated from its liability to pay compensation.

3. The brief facts of the case are that on 15.08.2008 at around 5:30 AM, deceased Harish along with his friend Suresh was travelling in an Indica NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:31803 2 MA-797-2012 Car bearing registration number MP-09-HD-2291 to Maihar for darshan.

When they reached near Semari on the Sohagpur main road, a truck bearing registration number MP-5-F-7315,
driven in a rash and negligent manner, collided with the Indica.
As a result, all the occupants of the car sustained grievous injuries and Harish succumbed to those injuries.
3.1 The claimants filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Harish.
The Claims Tribunal after recording evidence concluded that the accident was caused due to the fault of the insured vehicle, which resulted in Harish's death.
Consequently, a total compensation of Rs.13,36,328/- was awarded.
However, while awarding compensation, the Claims Tribunal exonerated the Insurance Company from liability of payment of Smt.Sharda And 3 Ors. vs Ramnath @ Santosh And 4 Ors.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the Claims Tribunal erred in treating the so called intimation of cancellation of the Insurance Policy dated 05.03.2008 marked as Ex. D-6 as valid,
since the same was never in fact issued to the owner and was never received by him.
4.1 He further submits that the proper intimation of cancellation of the Insurance Policy was in fact given only on 14.04.2010, whereas the accident occurred on 15.08.2008.
As such, prior to 14.04.2010, no intimation of cancellation had been given.

4.2 Apart from this, learned counsel also points out by referring to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:31803 3 MA-797-2012 provisions of Section 64VB of the Insurance Act that the requirement under the said provision is that the intimation of cancellation should be sent not only to the owner of the vehicle but also to the RTO.
However, no such intimation was sent and this fact has not been pleaded in defence by the Insurance Company.

In fact, during the cross-examination,
Pawan Kumar (DW-1), the witness of the Insurance Company admitted that no intimation was sent to the concerned Transport Authority.

4.3 He thus submits that the liability of the Insurance Company could not have been absolved by the Claims Tribunal and in any case, the liability to first pay and then recover ought to have been fastened upon the Insurance Company, keeping in view the fact that the claimants were third parties to the dispute between the owner and the insurer.
He, therefore, prays for allowing the appeal in the above terms.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that an Insurance Policy is a contract based on the consideration of payment of premium.

He further submits that since the contract is contingent upon the payment of such consideration, the Insurance Policy in the present case was issued on the promise of payment pursuant to the cheque in question.
Once the cheque was dishonoured, there was a complete absence of consideration; consequently, no valid contract came into existence.
Hence, the Insurance Company cannot be held liable for payment of compensation.

He, therefore, prays for dismissal of the appeal.
6.
Heard learned counsel for the respective parties and perused the record.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:31803 4 MA-797-2012 7.

Two facts are indisputable in the present case :
(i) that the Insurance Policy was issued on the promise of payment vide cheque in question Ex.D-1; and (ii) that the cheque was dishonoured.

However, the effect of dishonour of the cheque and the consequential cancellation of the policy has to be considered in light of the provisions of Sections 147 and 149 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The provision of Section 64 VB of the Insurance Act stipulates that no risk shall be assumed unless the premium is received in advance.
9. In the present case, although the premium was tendered in advance through cheque Ex. D-1, the cheque was subsequently dishonoured.

10. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Daddappa vs. National Insurance Company Ltd. in (2008)
2 SCC 595

Daddappa vs. National Insurance Company Ltd. in (2008)
2 SCC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
has considered all these aspects and observed in para 24 as under :
"24.

We are not oblivious of the distinction between the statutory liability of the insurance company vis--vis a third party in the context of Sections 147 and 149 of the Act and its liabilities in other cases.
But the same liabilities arising under a contract of insurance would have to be met if the contract is valid.
If the contract of insurance has been cancelled and all concerned have been intimated thereabout, we are of the opinion, the insurance company would not be liable to satisfy the claim."
11. It is thus clear that the consideration before the Hon'ble Apex Court was under identical circumstances.

The Hon'ble Apex Court after considering similar facts observed in para 24 that where the contract of insurance has been cancelled and all the concerned parties have been duly intimated thereof, the Insurance Company would not be liable to satisfy the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:31803 5 MA-797-2012 award.
12. In the present case, there was a complete absence of intimation prior to the occurrence of the accident on 15.08.2008.

13. In view of the above, although the cheque was dishonoured in light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, the Insurance Company can be fastened with liability to first pay the compensation and thereafter recover the same from the owner and driver of the vehicle.
14. Thus, it is hereby directed that the Insurance Company shall first pay the compensation as awarded by the Tribunal and may thereafter recover the same from the owner / driver of the vehicle.
15. With the aforesaid, the present appeal is hereby disposed off.
Certified copy as per rules.
(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Anushree Smt.
